primitives.name: Initial Failure Tolerance
primitives.verbatim_quote: So the would-be pitcher must remember that no description will enable him to curve the ball at his first attempts.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'t_f': 'time to first successful curve (days)', 'n_0': 'initial attempts before success (dimensionless)'}
primitives.assumptions: Learning follows exponential decay in success probability with increasing attempts.
primitives.breakdown_regime: t_f → ∞ for novice; t_f ≈ 1 day for expert.

primitives.name: Out-Curve Grip Mechanics
primitives.verbatim_quote: The simplest method is to take the ball in the hand between the extended thumb and the first and second fingers, the third and little finger being closed.
primitives.assumptions: Finger placement creates asymmetric contact torque for spin generation.
primitives.breakdown_regime: θ < π/6 leads to insufficient spin; θ > π/2 causes loss of control.

layer2.mapping: Grip mechanics mirror angular momentum transfer in rigid body dynamics.
layer2.telemetry: Torque applied via finger positioning during release.

primitives.name: Arm Swing Angle Derivative
primitives.verbatim_quote: In practising to acquire this curve, it is best to swing the arm not straight out, but bent at the elbow, with the ball just a little higher than the shoulder.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'α(t)': 'angular acceleration of arm (rad/s²)', 'θ(t)': 'arm swing angle (radians)', 'v(t)': 'ball velocity vector (m/s)'}
primitives.assumptions: Optimal trajectory requires time-varying angular acceleration profile.
primitives.breakdown_regime: α(t) = 0 implies no spin; α(t) > 10 rad/s² causes over-rotation.

layer2.mapping: Angular acceleration derivative governs spin axis orientation and Magnus effect magnitude.
layer2.telemetry: Rate of change of arm angle during delivery phase.
